title: Section 1: Narrative Tenses (Multiple Choice)
inst: Choose the correct verb tense (Past Simple, Past Continuous, or Past Perfect) to complete the story and the sentences.
theory:
Narrative Tenses Review:
- Past Simple: Main, completed, and consecutive actions in the past.
- Past Continuous: Long actions or actions in progress that were interrupted (while, when).
- Past Perfect: The 'oldest action', which happened BEFORE another action in the past (by the time, already, after).

items.q: 1. I ___ down the street when I suddenly heard a loud noise.
items.why: Action in progress interrupted by the noise (Past Continuous).

items.q: 2. By the time we arrived at the cinema, the movie ___.
items.why: The movie started BEFORE we arrived (Past Perfect).

items.q: 3. Yesterday, I woke up, ___ a quick shower, and left for work.
items.why: Sequence of short, consecutive past actions (Past Simple).

items.q: 4. While Sarah ___ her homework, her brother was playing video games.
items.why: Two actions in progress at the same time using 'while' (Past Continuous).

title: Section 2: The Bad Day (Story Completion)
inst: Write the verb in brackets in the correct narrative tense (Past Simple, Past Continuous, or Past Perfect).
theory: Pay attention to the context of the story to decide which tense to use.

items.q: 1. Last Monday, I ___ (have) a terrible day at the office.
items.why: Finished past action that introduces the story: had.

items.q: 2. I was exhausted because I ___ (not / sleep) well the night before.
items.why: Action that happened BEFORE Monday: hadn't slept / had not slept.

items.q: 3. While I ___ (prepare) a coffee in the kitchen, my boss called me.
items.why: Long interrupted action: was preparing.

items.q: 4. He asked me for the report, but I realized I ___ (forget) it at home!
items.why: Realized something that had happened BEFORE: had forgotten.

title: Section 1: Choose the Relative Pronoun
inst: Choose the correct relative pronoun (who, which, whose, where, when) for each sentence.
theory:
Relative Clauses Review:
- Who / That: For people.
- Which / That: For things or animals.
- Where: For places.
- When: For time.
- Whose: To indicate possession.

items.q: 1. That is the doctor ___ treated me when I broke my arm.
items.why: Refers to a person (the doctor).

items.q: 2. I can't find the folder ___ has all the important documents.
items.why: Refers to a thing (the folder).

items.q: 3. This is the hospital ___ my grandfather worked for 30 years.
items.why: Refers to a place where an action occurs (the hospital).

items.q: 4. Do you know the girl ___ brother won the gold medal?
items.why: Indicates possession: the girl's brother (whose).

title: Section 2: Combine the Sentences
inst: Combine the two sentences into one using a Relative Pronoun. Do not repeat the subject or the object!
theory:
Example:
The man is angry. His car is broken. -> The man whose car is broken is angry.

items.q:
1. The smartphone is very expensive. I bought it yesterday. (Use WHICH or THAT)
-> The smartphone ____________________________ is very expensive.
items.why: which/that I bought yesterday

items.q:
2. I met a woman. She works as a software engineer. (Use WHO or THAT)
-> I met a woman ____________________________.
items.why: who/that works as a software engineer

items.q:
3. That is the cafe. We had our first date there. (Use WHERE)
-> That is the cafe ____________________________.
items.why: where we had our first date

title: Section 1: Modals in Context
inst: Choose the correct modal verb to complete each sentence, paying attention to the context (obligation, prohibition, advice, or lack of obligation).
theory:
Modals Review:
- Must / Have to: Obligation (rules or necessity).
- Mustn't: Strict prohibition (do not do it).
- Don't have to: No obligation (you can do it if you want, but it's not necessary).
- Should / Ought to: Advice or recommendations.

items.q: 1. The sign says 'Private Property'. You ___ enter this area.
items.why: It is a strict prohibition indicated by a sign.

items.q: 2. Tomorrow is Sunday! I ___ wake up early.
items.why: Lack of obligation; it is not necessary to wake up early.

items.q: 3. You look very tired and sick. I think you ___ go to the doctor.
items.why: It is strong advice or a recommendation.

items.q: 4. In most offices, employees ___ wear a tie. It's the company rule.
items.why: It is an external obligation imposed by company rules.

title: Section 2: The Mega Integration (Key Word Transformations)
inst: The final challenge! Rewrite the sentences using the word in capital letters without changing the meaning. These sentences mix Past Tenses, Relatives, and Modals.
theory: Instructions: Use everything you have learned. Do not change the word in brackets.

items.q:
1. It is strictly prohibited for the students who study here to use phones.
-> The students who study here ____________________________ phones. (MUSTN'T)
items.why: mustn't use (Combines relatives with prohibition).

items.q:
2. My advice for the man whose car broke down is to take a taxi.
-> The man whose car broke down ____________________________ a taxi. (SHOULD)
items.why: should take (Combines relatives with advice).

items.q:
3. It was not necessary for me to read the book that the teacher recommended.
-> I ____________________________ the book that the teacher recommended. (HAVE)
items.why: didn't have to read (Combines lack of obligation in the PAST with a relative clause).

items.q:
4. While the doctor was examining the patient, it was a rule to wear gloves.
-> While the doctor was examining the patient, he ____________________________ gloves. (HAD)
items.why: had to wear (Combines past continuous with past obligation).
